artifacts.summary: Root-causes the artifacts[] shape ambiguity to .orchestrator-handoff.json (not .return-meta.json, which is already correctly pinned), identifies the missing Defensive-case guidance in lean-research-agent.md/lean-research-hard-agent.md, and recommends one-normative-place fixes plus flagged consumer-side and scope follow-ups.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent system, .return-meta.json's artifacts[] shape is strictly pinned (object required, four-layer enforcement) but .orchestrator-handoff.json's artifacts[] shape is only shown by worked example (JSON schema, wrap-up.md, handoff-schema.md) with no explicit 'never a bare string' prose sentence, and no validator actually checks element-level type. When auditing a schema-adjacent pair of files for ambiguity, check whether a prohibition is stated as an explicit negative sentence versus merely implied by a required-fields list -- the latter is what actually drifts in practice even when a JSON Schema structurally forbids it, because no ad hoc jq validator re-derives full JSON-Schema semantics.

Three agent contracts (general-research-agent.md, general-research-hard-agent.md, general-implementation-agent.md) already carry a 'Defensive case, if a handoff is written anyway' paragraph for the documented-never-but-sometimes-happens scenario of a base-mode/research agent being instructed to write .orchestrator-handoff.json. This is the correct established pattern to extend (not invent) when a new agent needs the same defensive guidance -- e.g. lean-research-agent.md and lean-research-hard-agent.md were found to have no such paragraph at all despite reproducing the exact scenario it exists to cover.
